intro: Sequence audits need explicit expected boundaries. Inferring the range from observed IDs would miss gaps before the first observed item or after the last.
task: Return missing integer sequence IDs between explicit inclusive bounds.
requirements: start and end are integers 0..1e9 with start <= end and end-start <= 1000. ids contains integers within that inclusive range; duplicates and unsorted IDs are allowed. Return all absent IDs in ascending order.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Build a membership set from observed IDs, then scan the explicit range.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: The end is inclusive; include end when it has not been observed.

explanation: Sequence audits need explicit expected boundaries. Inferring the range from observed IDs would miss gaps before the first observed item or after the last.
Duplicates do not fill additional sequence positions. A set removes repeated observations, while an ascending range provides deterministic missing-ID order.
